dimensions.statement: Audits four defect classes in an IPI evaluation harness and proposes measurement-valid scenarios; this is not a web-navigation retention experiment.

Attacker controls third-party email/file/SQL text; cannot modify trusted prompts, weights or defense configuration. Static versus defense-aware adaptive knowledge settings distinguished; reported experiments are static.
Structured file, email or SQL injection locator; tool-call mediation between proposed and executed actions.
Single-user tasks use read_email, send_email, read_file, write_file, execute_sql_query in sandboxed per-scenario environments; in-memory SQL effects observable.
gpt-5.6-terra; local llama3.1:8b, gemma4:12b, qwen2.5-coder:7b. Core/reduced/probe suites. Model identifiers are retained as source-reported, not independently verified deployments.

None, TypeChecker, CapabilityRouter and LLMJudge conditions. Identity versus argument scoring on identical traces; delivery needs a paired sweep. Model incapacity and environment mismatch confound utility/security.
Greedy where provider permits; per-scenario timeout stated without a numeric duration; Fisher exact, Holm correction and Wilson intervals. No numerical token/call/cost cap reported.
ASR is argument-constrained predicate on executed calls; UPR is coverage of required tool names, FRR=100-UPR on benign stratum. UPR is not independent end-state task verification.

95 core scenarios=43 attack+52 benign; reduced55=43+12; capability10. D2 re-score258 attack runs; D3 282 benign runs. Judge367 decisions. Exact aggregation into the ablation denominators is insufficiently specified.

Audited delivery4/43; corrected43/43. llama reading-tool exposure41/43. Structured placement and predicates plus persisted calls/results; reading-tool execution does not alone prove every payload token entered model context.
Sustained browser retention, semantic state recurrence and time-to-escape are NOT STUDIED; no zero-retention inference is warranted.
Rollback recovery is NOT STUDIED. Utility under attack is represented via required-tool coverage; it cannot substitute for a trusted task-progress oracle.
Per-scenario manifests/traces described. Numeric tokens, wall-time, calls and monetary budgets NOT REPORTED as study outcomes; deterministic TypeChecker has no inference cost by design.
Frontier none ASR2.3%, FRR7.7%; router ASR0%, FRR5.8%; judge ASR2.3%, FRR11.5%. These are paper-reported cells, not replication; no significant frontier defense differences reported.

Author says harness/code/tests released but withholds full attack suites/per-scenario results until archival version. No concrete repository URL appears in supplied text; availability and numerical reconstruction are unverified.

Table I prints D3 10.3->6.7 with +3.5pp; displayed values differ by3.6pp (rounding may explain). Text alternates39 undelivered/38 undelivered. FRR attribution to defense remains stronger than a required-tool metric can establish; single domain, static attacks and underpowered frontier cells.

Recommendation: validate delivery, scorer predicates and benign feasibility separately; retain complete traces and missingness. Require independent legitimate state/progress checks, stronger than tool coverage.
Joint attack/benign utility measurement is explicitly attributed to AgentDojo. Harness validity checks and exposure accounting are prior methodological requirements, not a novel trap contribution.
Combines agent fingerprinting and server-side cloaking as delivery for known prompt-injection risks; includes a small internal demonstration in section4.
Attacker controls web server and conditional content, knows agent/automation fingerprints; goal unauthorized actions with concealment.
User-agent/IP/ASN and automation/behavior cues drive differential page delivery; proposed hidden payload or entirely different authentication page.
Benign API-documentation access becomes a prerequisite to authenticate using an environment variable; Cursor agent has shell/local-secret access, stronger than ordinary browser-only delegated tasks.
Internal website with server-side detection; Cursor powered by Claude4 Sonnet, GPT-5 Fast and Gemini2.5 Pro. Model/version strings are source-reported only.
Benign-human versus agent-authentication flow illustrated, but randomized matched controls, assignment rules and repeated-trial outcomes NOT REPORTED.
No trial protocol, retry schedule, resource cap or sampling plan reported beyond testing the internal page with three listed models.
States attack succeeded in all cases; successful secret-authentication flow illustrated. No formal success predicate, exfiltration verification rule or benign completion rubric reported.
Three named model configurations are listed; number of trials per configuration and denominator for all cases NOT REPORTED. Do not reconstruct n=3 or an ASR estimate.
Author-reported internal implementation; Figure1 contrasts benign and malicious flows. No raw execution traces or measured classifier sensitivity/specificity supplied.
Sustained retention, recurrent prerequisites and exit-time measurements NOT STUDIED as outcomes; this is targeted delivery and a reported credential prerequisite demonstration.
Task completion is part of proposed concealment; recovery/rollback or independent progress after compromise NOT EVALUATED.
Tokens, calls, browser actions, latency and monetary costs NOT REPORTED.
Fingerprint randomization, input sanitization, planner/executor isolation, anti-cloaking crawlers and honeypot agents proposed; no measured mitigation comparison in this source.
Internal website described; no supplied reusable implementation, data or trace artifact identity. Citations to other systems do not establish availability of this implementation.

Broad stealth/scalability/reliability claims exceed demonstrated scope; no detection accuracy, trial denominators, controlled effectiveness or independent reproduction. Browser/shell privileges and visibility assumptions limit generalization. Section3.3 p.6 assumes full-HTML ingestion and local-browser-data access; these are threat-model assumptions, not universal browser-agent capabilities. Section3.2 p.5 explicitly allows an entirely different malicious page; visually identical delivery is not required by the demonstration.

Recommendation: record exactly what agent and human inspectors receive; preserve server-side response and observation identities. Keep browser-only and shell/local-secret privileges in separate threat-model tiers.

Agent-targeted differential content and authentication pretexts are prior art. A conceptual framing cannot support claimed prevalence or general effectiveness; internal demonstration does not establish sustained trapping.
Termination poisoning corrupts progress assessment to continue execution after legitimate completion; automated target profiling and task-specific payload synthesis.

Can modify external content; knows task type; no system-prompt/memory/weight access or code/tool/orchestration modification; payload fixed during victim execution. Across-attempt feedback in optimization is a distinct interface.
Pages, retrieved documents, API returns, shared files/skills described. Main experiments inject through simulated tool returns, not a validated live hostile website.
GAIA-style legitimate research/tool tasks; shared ReAct scaffold. Final answer/stop criterion can be delayed through purported checking and dependency requirements.
Eight model engines in one unified main scaffold, 60 sampled GAIA tasks; main environment simulates tool returns; LangChain/LangGraph comparison is in AppendixC p.15.

Clean baseline; ten static strategies; Static-Random/Rotate-All/LLM-Direct/Static-Best/NoProfile/LoopTrap. Same tasks for profiling-characterization/evaluation; reflection-removal also lowers attempts, confounding component attribution.

Four clean+four injected probe executions. Twenty episodes per agent-task pair; M3 refinements and n3 candidates; ten repeats in adaptive evaluation. Per-trial step ceiling mentioned pp.14-15 without numerical value.
SAF=Tprime/T; ASR uses alpha2. Strict > versus inclusive >= conflicts; Figure11 labels2.0x successful. Final-answer correctness and verified non-progress are not the success endpoint.
Initial60 tasks x10 strategies x5 repetitions=3000/model. Eight models. Adaptive20 episodes/pair with10 independent runs; no reconstructed exact successful-trial counts from rounded ASR.
Study assumes a modified source is encountered; simulation controls tool delivery. Live exposure/search-discovery probability and independent token-level delivery verification NOT REPORTED.

P7 recursive verification and P8 circular prerequisites explicitly defined. Illustrative tasks terminate with finite2-4x amplification; aggregate SAF3.57x, ASR86.3% (Table4 p.11); token3.93x (Table6 p.16). These are not literal nontermination or post-entry time-to-escape.

Independent progress/goal oracle and measured escape/rollback recovery NOT EVALUATED. Proposed independent progress verification is future work pp.12-13. Figure11 changes final answer Bravo->Hercules.
Reports SAF/TAF and episode-to-success; SAF3.57x and TAF3.93x aggregate. No billing audit, measured wall time or complete generator+victim query accounting. Peak25x lacks trace-level identification.
Independent progress verification and provenance-aware processing proposed, not evaluated adaptive defenses.
AppendixB asserts anonymous code/probe/skill/simulator package. Repository/code/raw outcomes not supplied to this analysis; availability and implementation correspondence unverified.

Unresolved model rankings, profile scores, seven versus fourteen categories, NoProfile averages/SAF, strategy frequencies totaling110%, SAF/CAF label, strict/inclusive boundary and changed-answer case. Retain original values, no silent correction.

Recommendation: distinguish useful checking from verified non-progress; record exact observations and completion; separately measure entry/retention/recovery. Prespecify boundary, caps, repeat units and full attacker/victim budgets.

No novelty claim for circular dependencies, task-specific verification loops, poisoned termination, profiling/adaptive synthesis or proposed independent progress verification. Narrower page-only semantic x recurrence causal test still requires competitor review.
Explicit model-directed multi-step rollback for benign web navigation; decides when and where to return rather than only greedy forward actions or highest-value switching.
NOT APPLICABLE: no adversarial attacker condition. Erroneous or unpromising navigation states are benign failures.
Agent framework adds critique and rollback modules, with recorded URLs and navigation history; environment is represented via accessibility trees.
Mind2Web-Live and WebVoyager user tasks; click/type/scroll/wait/goback/restart/stop. Rollback picks an earlier step index.
Zero-shot Llama3.3-70B-Instruct/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct; fine-tuned Llama3.1-8B-Instruct/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; GPT4o and mini subset; GPT4o evaluator.

OneWay, BestFirst and Rollback comparisons. Rollback uses fewer state switches than BestFirst; extra model critique/rollback calls are distinct from browser navigation steps. Website filtering and judge validity constrain conclusions.
Default navigation budget16 steps; experiments repeated3 times; budget scaling8/16/24/32 on randomly chosen100-instance subset. Additional calls/cost caps NOT REPORTED.
Full task completion and partial0-1 judge score; average steps and switches; struggle-ratio is proportion requiring recovery. No adversarial ASR or trap-retention endpoint.

Filtered test sets42 Mind2Web-Live and342 WebVoyager;455 training instances. Closed-model results use100 randomly selected subset; repeated3 times. Do not substitute full benchmark sizes for filtered denominators.
No malicious exposure/delivery condition. Agent navigation trajectories support benign outcome judging; no trust-boundary attack verification.
Repeated unproductive benign actions motivate rollback; no sustained hostile retention/time-to-escape distribution measured. Browser state switches are not proof of productive recovery.

Algorithm1 requests env.rollback(S[i]); actual implementation records each step URL and resets browser to selected URL. This is not a demonstrated general transaction/session/database undo. Appendix p.9 restricts return destinations to [Checkpoint Saved] steps; this need not mean every previous state is available.
Navigation-step and state-switch averages reported. Struggle-ratio19% OneWay vs7% Rollback. No full token, wall-time or monetary accounting; fewer browser steps do not establish fewer model calls.
Rollback is benign capability intervention, not a tested security defense; adversarial critique poisoning and irreversible state restoration NOT EVALUATED.
Prompts in appendicesB/C and dataset links in AppendixD; Playwright and OpenRLHF dependencies cited. Linked dependencies do not establish release of a complete implementation/trace package.

Live-site availability filtering limits external validity. GPT4o judge uses inferred partial progress; evaluation prompt can accept unsupported final-response content when absent from tree. URL restore cannot prove full state restoration. Untuned small-model appendix results include ties and BestFirst advantages; main-table superiority is not universal. Algorithm1 leaves initial S population implicit; this is documentary incompleteness, not a proven runtime bug.
Recommendation: specify recovery interface and restored state components; verify post-rollback legitimate progress independently; account for critique/model costs and irreversible actions.

Explicit multi-step rollback, when/where decisions and efficiency-versus-recovery comparisons are prior art. Proposed trap research must test adversarial recovery without claiming rollback itself new.
Honeyval evaluates LLM HTTP honeypots using main agent-honeypot interactions plus independent agent exploit and honeypot functional controls.
Honeypot defender simulates HTTP API responses without underlying system-resource access. Evaluated adversary is an AI hacking agent assigned a concrete exploit goal; both know the full API spec.
Hollow HTTP server routes API requests to a prompted LLM. Response content/state simulation, not browser-only DOM text, is controlled.
Task is exploit real/decoy APIs (script download, database-table deletion, admin-password change or browser local-storage exfiltration). This is not ordinary delegated-user browsing.
16 BaxBench-derived backend apps; ReAct curl/python agents with Gemini3 Flash or Claude Sonnet4.6; GeminiCLI and ClaudeCode. Five honeypot backends listed in Table1.
LLM vs rule-based honeypots; agent controls on secure/insecure real implementations; honeypot functionality tests. Same configuration across main/control tasks, with prompt adaptation comparisons.
Five independent repetitions; agent and LLM honeypot each$10/run. ReAct50 iterations; ClaudeCode/GeminiCLI1h/run. Caps differ in units and censor realized interaction lengths.
HTTP request count, running costs, honeypot-detection TPR/FPR, exploit verifier callbacks on real apps, functional pass@1. No exploit can succeed against resource-free honeypot by construction.
16backend apps and5 repetitions. Do not infer one pooled independent sample count across agent/backend/prompt/control configurations; distinguish each table cell and test denominator.
Programmatic exploit verification on real apps; detection judged by agent reports/abort. Request count verifies interaction, not hostile instruction uptake or ordinary user-task non-progress.
Mean request engagement82.6 LLM vs30.6 rule baseline in reported aggregate. Table3 None/CarefulPI/Convince lengths82.6/50.1/102.6. Endpoint is HTTP requests, not browser actions or survival time.
Agent may declare honeypot and exit or give up; exploit utility control tests real apps. Escape declaration is not independently verified completion after trap entry; rollback recovery NOT STUDIED.

Author-reported: Table2 median latency3.3–13.7s and generated tokens87.7–523.9; Table3 baseline-prompt cost advantage3.6x. Full context is resubmitted per request while agents may batch requests. AppendixB p.12 estimates API cost from input/output/cache tokens but omits higher long-context pricing tiers. Analyst interpretation: a nominal $10-per-side limit is not an independently verified strict billed ceiling.
Convince length102.6 vs82.6 but TPR0.45 vs0.24; CarefulPI length50.1, TPR0.49 and fidelity0.62 vs0.84 baseline. Added deception objectives can harm stealth/fidelity.
Paper gives https://github.com/google-research/honeyval; describes specs, real secure/insecure implementations, tests and callbacks. Artifact content not executed/reproduced here.

Impossible exploit goal on decoy differs from solvable legitimate task with reachable escape. Prompt/cap/cost asymmetries and agent-type differences constrain transfer to proposed website traps. Requests/calls/time not interchangeable.

Recommendation: separate victim competence, environment fidelity, retention, detection and utility controls. Fix prompt variants and budgets; preserve assigned-episode and conditional-entry denominators.

AI-agent engagement, deception prompts and retention-versus-detectability/cost tradeoffs are prior art. New study cannot claim first agent-retaining decoy; must distinguish solvable browser tasks and independently measured recovery.
Login-inducing page-context attack leads from plausible prerequisite to controlled sensitive-information form.
Controls cloned page/popup and login destination; knows neither actual user task nor agent/model/system prompt/safety policy; no runtime modification or internal reasoning access.
Popup contains login rationale, forged entry and close button; contextualized local login page. Two shadow evaluators filter statements, not final victim success.
Ordinary Mind2Web-derived tasks with synthetic background information. Agent clicks/types/navigates; sensitive values come from supplied background.
80 cloned pages/1175 tasks/five domains. Browser-Use with GPT4o/Gemini3Flash/ClaudeSonnet4/DeepSeekV3.2; GPT4o fixed for Browser-Use/LiteWebAgent/Skyvern comparison.

Varies backbone or architecture while fixing other comparison axis. No reported clean-page outcomes, popup-only control or component ablation; local cloning and unknown system versions confound transfer.
Fresh Chrome/reset per execution; all experiments max5 interaction steps. PER uses3 sampled tasks x3 repetitions=9attempts/page. Numerical generation budget NOT REPORTED.

LER is forged-entry click; ASR is entry then sensitive-information input. Submission and network-received leakage are not consistently mandatory. PER is any successful attempt within9, distinct from per-run probability.

Dataset80pages/1175tasks; PER9attempts/page. Exact task-level outcome counts and headline averaging weights NOT REPORTED. Figure6 gives page counts supporting derived80/80,75/80,79/80 across architectures.

Observable browser actions/navigation/form inputs when available label entry and ASR using synthetic background values. No inference from hidden reasoning; shadow predictions are not victim action verification.
Five-step credential-diversion flow; sustained browser retention, semantic recurrence and post-completion amplification NOT EVALUATED.
Paper qualitatively mentions incomplete form filling, early stop and return to task; no quantified recovery oracle or rollback experiment. LER->ASR gap is not a sustained-retention estimate.
Agent step5 and PER attempt9 caps reported. Tokens, total generator calls, wall-time and financial costs NOT REPORTED.
Task-instruction/system-prompt/action-supervision defenses claimed to reduce but not eliminate leakage; detailed configurations and numerical results absent. Do not rank defenses.
Source describes local clone/login construction and browser logs; no supplied release URL, code, dataset or trace package. External artifact availability not verified.

Clonability selection, synthetic sensitive data, five-step cap, repeated tasks nested in pages, absent uncertainty and unspecified aggregate weights limit generality. Input is not automatically submitted exfiltration.

Recommendation: separate page-context relevance from actual task knowledge; distinguish entry, input, submission, received effect and recovery. Provide legitimate close/escape route and source-defined denominators.

Plausible login prerequisite and coherent multi-step malicious continuation are established prior art; a first prerequisite/login trap claim is unsupported. Retention must be measured separately from credential diversion.
ABxLab uses observation interventions to study consumer choice, not a security attack benchmark.
NOT APPLICABLE as malicious attacker objective: nudges intentionally influence choice; framework operator can intercept/modify observations.
Man-in-middle observation function modifies product-title-adjacent text and matched prices in pruned viewport HTML, with no visual input.
Select better of two products and add to cart; nine browser actions; explicit short-term thoughts/memory; stop on cart addition or10 actions.
OneStopMarket/AgentLab/WebArena-derived environment;17 model engines;50 product pairs; original human baseline and secondary6-model subsets.

No nudge/first product nudged/second product nudged. Original vs matched ratings(MR) vs matched ratings+prices(MRaP). Pairs category-constrained; matched set differs from original set; order randomized. Matching does not remove all product-description confounds.
Temperature0.1 where available,1 for OpenAI reasoning models;10-action cap; cluster-robust linear probability estimates, logit robustness and BH correction.
Endpoint is chosen product/cart addition and marginal change in choice probability in percentage points. No harmful-action ASR, sustained retention or escape endpoint.

Ten interventions x50pairs x3conditions=1500 base configurations; >80000 experiments,~2.5B tokens,~400k requests. Human30participants x50 decisions=1500 choices; do not infer identical agent/human UI trajectories.

Observation intervention and cart action determine exposure/choice; framework makes synthetic nudges available. Visible HTML is different from full DOM and screenshots; no measured attack-payload delivery chain.
Recurrence/retention NOT STUDIED as attack outcomes; episodes terminate after choice or10actions. Product-choice bias is not proof of being trapped.
Rollback, escape and post-entry legitimate recovery NOT STUDIED; correct preference satisfaction is not an independent trap-progress metric here.
Global approximate2.5B tokens/~400k requests reported; do not derive per-episode averages from rounded totals or treat them as complete cost caps.
Explicit user preference profiles are behavioral conditions; no demonstrated trap defense. Preference adherence and nudge susceptibility do not establish security or utility under attack.
Paper identifies abxlab.media.mit.edu and an open framework/benchmark; claimed artifacts require separate content/version verification, no experiments executed here.

Forced binary choice, no visual observations, selected catalog, title filtering and different pair construction constrain generality; large behavioral effects are not a universal agent-human vulnerability multiplier. Original-to-MR changes pair/category composition; negative-nudge inversion and underspecified user priorities further limit normative harm interpretations. Generated thinking/memory is not independently faithful (pp.24-25).

Recommendation: use matched stimuli/counterfactual observation changes, randomized order, cluster-aware units and controlled factual utility. Separately manipulate task relevance and recurrence while holding topology/affordances fixed.

Controlled webpage/observation nudges, framing comparisons and attribute matching are established methodology. New trap contribution must identify a distinct outcome/causal contrast, not merely renamed persuasion.
Entry-Propagation-Recovery(EPR) diagnoses how retrieved memories change action trajectories; compliance trap is uptake of plausible task-wrong memory followed by low success/recovery.
Intervention controls retrieved textual memory content and injection timing. This is a memory-consumption experiment, not demonstrated page-only attacker access.

Helpful/conflicting/cross-task memory in matched DO/DONT templates; early step1/persistent every step/late from step3. Primary system-prompt injection and observation-footer placement comparison are controlled memory insertion; similar effects do not establish a real webpage-only attacker delivery chain.
BrowserGym AXTree tasks on WebArena and MemTrapBench; legitimate goal has task-correct and known decoy paths in constructed benchmark.

Five models named in main WebArena protocol; main MemTrapBench Table3 reports four. Full684 non-map precheck, selected77 diagnostic subset,231 constructed main tasks, plus611 common-valid cross-family and MiniWoB controls. Preserve model/cohort-specific denominators.

Paired no-memory baseline with same seed; fixed content varied availability; helpful/conflicting length/structure-matched and cross-task controls. WebArena subset selected on two Qwen outcomes; MemTrapBench constructed separately with hand verification claimed.

Paired same-seed early/persistent/late schedules, greedy decoding; 10000 sign-flip and bootstrap iterations. Appendix p.14 specifies 15 browser steps, 600 seconds per trajectory, 8192-token context and max 2048 generated tokens; vLLM v0.19 on A6000 48GB, bfloat16, prefix caching, temperature0/top-p1. Gemini uses API temperature0.

WebArena RCR is LLM-judge recommendation compliance at first exposure; DPC paired success difference on compliant subset. Main MemTrapBench Table3 DPC instead uses action-divergence subset. Do not pool these selected conditional measures or treat them as randomized entry effects.
WebArena77 eligible diagnostic tasks; Table2 model validN75/67/77/75/77 and compliant47/42/53/54/51; figure caption Gemini n74 differs. Do not use full684 as diagnostic denominator.

Known schedule establishes memory availability. Judge compares first exposed action with recommendation and paired action. Divergence alone is not compliance; groundability gate distinguishes absent AXTree labels.

Persistent conflicting memory produces more harm than early on selected models. RCR63-72%, compliance-conditioned success17-31%; Figure4 realignment7-15% conflicting vs27-42% helpful. Caption says cumulative divergence by7, prose by14.

EPR explicitly separates correction/realignment from task-level recovery; paired no-memory reference and known constructed trap path support diagnosis. These measures are prior art, not a new proposed trap metric by themselves.

Step/trajectory analyses and explicit 15-step/600-second caps with 8192-context/2048-generation limits are supplied, but no complete per-condition token/call/currency ledger. Browser actions, generated tokens and wall time are separate units.

Caution wording trades helpful gain for less conflicting harm. Retry-on-fail compares first no-memory attempt with helpful-memory retry after observed failure; requires failure signal and extra attempt. Schedule oracle has outcome access; both are diagnostic, not demonstrated deployable controller gains.
Task/memory blueprints and audits described in appendices; external code/data release and independent execution not verified here.

Outcome-selected WebArena77, varying validN, main/appendix and caption/prose discrepancies remain. Table29 printed recovery22/40/35% differs from caption35-40%; no-memory gains2.0/2.6/2.7 differ from stated2.6-5.6. Grounding/entry factorial interaction is small relative to main effects (Table23 p.23), limiting a simple multiplicative-gate reading. Appendix p.14 calls Gemini MemTrap-only although WebArena tables include it; model and denominator scope must follow individual tables.

Recommendation: distinguish entry/compliance, propagation, trajectory realignment and independently verified completion. Use paired seeds, matched irrelevant/helpful controls and prespecified exposure schedules; selection on compliance remains conditional/descriptive.

EPR, repeated misleading-memory exposure, known-correct-path diagnosis and recovery/utility analysis are prior art. AppendixE Table23 p.23 already tests identifiability x action-groundability2x2 (32tasks/cell/model); proposed semantics x recurrence must establish a distinct contrast rather than claim first factorial trap study.
WebStep evaluates process-level web-agent behavior through deterministic semantic MDPs behind GUI websites.
NOT APPLICABLE: benign evaluation, no adversarial attacker; evaluator controls self-hosted world, distractors and task generation.

GUI frontend renders from semantic state. AppendixC/Table3 p.17: Claude receives screenshot+interactive DOM with reference targeting/coordinate fallback; other evaluated agents are pixel-only. Do not attribute all differences solely to model capability.
Find unique target under constraints and execute commit;10 synthetic sites/1800 tasks with oracle trajectories, hard negatives and controlled information access.
Fara7B, GUI-Owl1.5-8B, UI-TARS1.5-7B, Qwen3.5-122B, OpenAI CUA(GPT5.4), Claude CUA(Sonnet4.6); chosen workshop version.
Agent/model comparisons and complexity strata; shared semantic states permit successful/failing trace alignment. No randomized hostile semantic-framing treatment.
Maximum50 GUI turns/task; source documents model-specific decoding. Environment deterministic conditional on seed/actions, not all model outputs deterministic.

Main terminal/exploration/conditional-execution/coverage/step metrics are qualified by AppendixC.3 p.18: ALL terminal success uses SafePass, accepting sufficiently informed correct decision points without final commit. Ready-to-act differs from executed goal completion. Skill invocation is not skill success (p.7).
1800 task instances on10 websites; Table2 provides agent aggregates. Bifurcation Figure5 n-values count classified behaviors/trace units; do not interpret them as new independent task trials.
Semantic source-of-truth couples GUI updates to typed state transitions; automatic oracle replay/testing plus manual checks described. Delivery of hostile text NOT STUDIED.

Bifurcation is last shared state before divergence: wrong branch(neither next action commit), delayed commit(successful next commit), premature commit(failing next commit). Benign delayed completion is not attacker-caused retention.

Semantic observer supports process diagnosis, but SafePass does not require final commit. Table22 p.35 shows seven-action oracle alongside successful4/3-action traces, qualifying global minimum claims. Case7 p.48 distinguishes guardrail stop from standard failure. Adversarial recovery NOT EVALUATED.

50-turn episode cap; open-model output maxima800 or2048 tokens (Table3). FourH200(140GB each) node for GPU models; full GPU evaluation approximately3-4days; each closed agent within1day with8workers(p.17). GUI and semantic counts differ; no complete per-condition token/currency ledger.
NOT APPLICABLE as security defense comparison. Process diagnosis and skill weaknesses do not establish a trap mitigation.
Reproducibility statement says full benchmark will be released:10sites/1800definitions/world seeds/oracles/evaluation suite. Future release statement is not inspected artifact availability.

Workshop/public arXiv abstract mismatch retained. SafePass modifies actual completion; Claude DOM assistance confounds modality; oracles are not established globally shortest. Coverage non-discriminative for226/1800 initially satisfied tasks(p.18). Synthetic sites and disabled external actions constrain transfer.

Recommendation: independent semantic progress oracle and explicit state/action transitions; distinguish exploration failure, delayed commit and premature stop; test solvable benign iterations and validate all exits.

Semantic state tracking, oracle trajectories, progress-based diagnosis and bifurcation localization are prior art. Proposed study must contribute a new causal comparison/outcome, not claim first process evaluation.
Studies machine-readable ad accessibility and observable trust patterns on a cloned news website; not an adversarial prompt-injection efficacy study.
NOT APPLICABLE as attacker objective. Study operator modifies ads/markup and supplied prompts; commercial persuasion need not be malicious instruction injection.
Manipulates semantic DOM buttons, offscreen spans, ARIA/data/alt attributes, placement, dynamic media, native dialogs and subscription/paywall framing.
Ten authored tasks cover subscription, coupon, sweepstakes, news and consent behavior. Relevant prompts include fictitious personal/payment data.
BrowserUse0.1.41 with GPT4o/Claude3.7Sonnet/Gemini2.0Flash; additional pixel-based Operator explorations June1-15,2025; cloned TirolerTageszeitung site.
Identical initial prompts/UI/defaults for BrowserUse. Follow-up markup/media variants; Operator differs in action/confirmation/instrumentation, so cross-paradigm comparison is indicative.

Each10 tasks x10repeats per3 BrowserUse models=300 baseline trials. Followups10trials/model/condition; reset sessions; connectivity/render failures excluded. Complete realized denominator and numeric step/time cap NOT REPORTED.
Observed ad clicks, coupon finding, scroll depth, cookies and subscription selection; human manually records Operator. No composite trust score, malicious ASR or sustained-trap endpoint.
Baseline300 plus followups; TableIII10 trials/model/variant; TableIV10/model/strategy. Cookie30trials/banner variant. Subscription conditional denominators23/30/27 are not300.
BrowserUse action JSON/final answer/screen GIF logs; Operator manually annotated. Hidden semantic span can affect agents despite visual invisibility; observation visibility must be documented.
Deep coupon at virtualpage10 not reached; TableVI maxscroll3/2/5 by model. Broad never-beyond-two-viewports phrasing requires qualification. Early stopping does not demonstrate sustained retention.
Escape/rollback recovery NOT STUDIED. Goal-contingent payment choices and incomplete search are distinct from a verified non-progress trap.
Action and scroll counts reported; no full per-condition tokens/calls/latency/currency accounting. Operator cost/latency/confirmation differ qualitatively.
DOMbutton overlays7/10 Claude and GPT,5/10 Gemini versus pixeltext0/10; offscreen span9/10,10/10,10/10. These are accessibility outcomes, not tested security defenses.
Development stack and BrowserUse dependency cited; no independently inspected full clone/data/rawtrace release. Do not treat tool URLs as artifact verification.

Gemini subscription tiers5+0+20=25 with denominator27; unresolved remaining2. Oneclone, dummycredentials, modeldrift, followups and modality confounding. Goal-contingent purchases do not establish actual financial loss.
Recommendation: log actual observation extraction; match visual/DOM affordances and cost justification; use consent/utility controls. Do not assume hidden DOM text is delivered to every agent.
Semantic overlays, offscreen text and goal-contingent purchase pretexts are precedent for observation/framing effects; they are not evidence of new sustained adversarial trapping.
Hierarchical diagnosis separates high-level planning, low-level execution, postcondition checking and replanning in benign web tasks.
NOT APPLICABLE: no attacker tested. Benchmarked errors are reliability failures, not demonstrated adversarial manipulation.
Text-based DOM observations feed planning/execution and LLM postcondition checking; natural-language versus PDDL plan representations compared.
Mind2Web-Live tasks with expert key nodes converted into reviewed high-level plans; actions vary across Expanded, ActionObject and ActionID settings.
104 test instances; gpt5nano primary actor/evaluator; ClaudeHaiku4.5 and GeminiFlash2.5 additional actors with gpt5nano evaluation.
Human/NL/PDDL plans,3 action settings, before/after one replanning round. Human-derived plans provide capability control; no equal-budget adversarial treatment.
One replanning round; exact execution/prompt details in appendices. Main methods do not provide full token/wall/currency caps. Extra exploration/replanning budget must be accounted for.
Plan alignment rates, subgoal/plan completion, task success, action validity/hallucinated links/repetition/redundancy. Judges assess postconditions/final task; metrics have different denominators.
